newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S.Africa's Manuel says gold not encouraging.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S.Africa's Manuel says gold not encouraging.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Tuesday the short term outlook for gold was not encouraging following its fall below US$370 an ounce.

The sale of gold by European central banks aiming to meet Maastricht requirements for hard currency reserves and the Swiss National Bank's decision to reduce its gold holdings were both pushing the gold price lower, Manuel told Reuters.
The likelihood of gold sales by the International Monetary Fund was also a depressing factor, he said.
"The short term prospect for the gold price is certainly not very encouraging for gold producing countries like ours," he said at the National Trade and Investment Conference here.
Manuel said South Africa aimed to reduce its reliance on gold in the longer term.
"As a country, macroeconomic policy is premised on boosting our non-gold exports," he said.
"We can't place an over-reliance on what is clearly a diminishing commodity," he said.
Manuel said the South African Reserve Bank also had gold reserves but the bank managed those reserves independently and he did not want to comment on what they might do.
"They very very jealously guard their constitutional independence with respect to managing their reserves," he said.
